transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Start: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT)
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Shah, Marco Alvarez (Redwood) — Maya Torres, Liam O'Connor, Evelyn Park, Ravi Menon (Veridian)

Summary (auto): procurement + security alignment; primary ask: private deployment with customer-managed KMS; need MSA redlines and SLA commitments; finance needs pricing bands and trial metrics.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have a packed agenda — procurement playbook, the MSA/DPA redline ask from Maya, and then a technical quickwalk on KMS options with Ravi.
[00:18] Maya: Thanks Jordan. Yes we wanted to make sure we get alignment so our governance team can move this through cir- circle, uh approval for Q3 work. We have three gating items: data residency and DPA, key custody, and clear SLA/uptime definitions tied to pricing.
[00:35] Liam: And from security perspective we are leaning toward customer-managed keys. We can't accept split knowledge KMS hosted by vendor without HSM attestations, right.
[00:50] Priya: Totally get that, Liam. Redwood supports a few patterns — hosted KMS, customer Cloud KMS with BYOK, and on-prem HSM integrations for private deployments. We can show the technical tradeoffs in a minute.
[01:10] Evelyn: Quick question on pricing — Finance needs rough monthly cost at 100M tokens/month and at 1B tokens/month so we can see the commit curve. Also any egress fees?
[01:25] Jordan: We'll provide a tiered pricing table; the commit discount banding is standard — we can prelim with ballpark numbers now and formal quote after legal route. Egress depends on deployment type — hosted might have minimal, private will depend on peering/egress paths.
[01:40] Maya: For the MSA, our counsel called out two problematic clauses: the data retention paragraph and the indemnity carveout around regulatory investigations. We need either tighter language or a controlled escalation path.
[01:52] Jordan: Noted. We typically accept reasonable carveouts or a 30-day cure period. We'll propose a compromise redline.
[02:06] Ravi: On the technical side, if you want customer-managed keys in a private deployment, we'll need VPC peering and an HSM-backed KMS. That implies network egress patterns and extra latency maybe a couple milliseconds, but seems within SLOs if we co-locate regionally.
[02:28] Priya: Also the runtime can be configured to keep KV cache ephemeral and never persist to disk; that helps the DPA. There are options to rotate keys every X hours, but that increases cold-starts for large context models.
[02:45] Liam: What about attestation? We need SOC2 plus the KMS vendor's FIPS or HSM attestation.
[02:53] Marco: We can provide the SOC2 report and a KMS whitepaper; for HSM attestation we can either bring our own HSM integration playbook or point to cloud provider's certs.
[03:05] Maya: On SLAs — our SRE wants a 99.9% uptime for API endpoints and a 95th percentile latency under 250ms for token generation for sync calls. Do you track p95 per-route?
[03:20] Priya: Yes we have per-route p50/p95 and token-level breakdowns in Console. For dedicated pools we can guarantee p95 targets in the SLA; hosted has a slightly looser SLA but better burst capacity. There's also automatic fallback policy if a model variant is unavailable.
[03:35] Evelyn: Is there penalty language? Our procurement team prefers service credits tied to missed uptime targets.
[03:42] Jordan: We can include service credits; amount and caps are negotiable per contract tier. We'll flag the standard language in the MSA.
[03:55] Maya: Data residency — we must have logs and audit trails retained for 7 years for regulatory reasons. Is that doable?
[04:04] Marco: Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM; retention policies can be set per agreement for longer retention, but there may be an extra fee for >2 year cold storage.
[04:18] Liam: Who has access to those logs at Redwood? We need RBAC controls, and SSO/SAML into Console with SCIM provisioning.
[04:26] Priya: We support SSO SAML and SCIM, role mapping, and fine-grained RBAC. Access for Redwood engineers to customer-specific resources is audit-logged and can be blocked except in emergencies with an approval workflow.
[04:40] Ravi: On peering — we'll provide our VPC CIDR blocks and the expected egress NAT ranges. Do you support private link or VPC peering?
[04:48] Priya: Both. We commonly do VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. Private Link is supported in some regions. We'll pull region-by-region options in the follow-up doc.
[05:02] Maya: For DPA — can you confirm you won't use or train on our data? This is non-negotiable.
[05:11] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include a clause: no training or model improvement using customer input unless explicitly opted in. We'll also add a data handling appendix.
[05:24] Evelyn: Finance also needs to understand invoice cadence, early termination fees, and refund on unused committed credits.
[05:34] Jordan: Standard practice: monthly invoices against committed usage, true-up at quarter end, prorated refunds only in specific cases. We'll surface the exact billing language.
[05:50] Liam: A little point — for incident response, we need a 24/7 pager and an escalation matrix with SLOs for response times.
[05:58] Marco: We have a 24/7 ops channel for enterprise SLAs, with defined Sev1/Sev2 response times; we can include contact numbers in the contract appendix.
[06:10] Priya: Quick tech note on benchmarks: for your planned workloads (mostly short form tokenization with some chat), we expect token costs to drop with prefix caching and quantized kernels. The chosen model variant and sequence lengths will materially change cost.
[06:30] Ravi: We'll share a sample production prompt set and peak QPS so you can model costs.
[06:36] Jordan: Perfect — that's on the next steps list.
[06:45] Maya: Back to MSA redlines — can you provide a few options on KMS language: 1) vendor-managed, 2) customer-managed cloud KMS, 3) customer HSM onsite. We'll want to see obligations and responsibility matrix for each.
[06:59] Jordan: Yes we will prepare a KMS options appendix with responsibilities and expected timelines for each.
[07:08] Evelyn: Last question — any known export control/regulatory caveats for APAC customers vs EU?
[07:15] Priya: Data transfer rules will vary; we have regional control planes and can restrict data residency. For export controls we'll surface known limitations in the compliance pack.
[07:30] Maya: Great — sounds like we have a path. Can we lock a follow-up legal-only session next week to go through redlines?
[07:37] Jordan: Absolutely — we proposed 2027-05-14 09:00 PT in the next steps.
[07:44] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:47] Liam: Thanks.
[07:49] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings around acronyms (HSM attestation transcribed as "H S M attestation"), some filler words removed.
